content.title: About
content.content: Beef curry with rice is a fragrant dish that combines tender pieces of beef simmered in a spiced curry sauce with fluffy white rice. The curry blend typically includes turmeric, cumin, coriander, and ginger, giving the dish a rich flavor and golden hue.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Curry originates from Indian cuisine but has countless regional variations worldwide.
Slow cooking beef in curry sauce makes the meat exceptionally tender and flavorful.
It is traditionally served with basmati rice, which soaks up the sauce and retains the aroma.
Some versions add coconut milk for a creamier texture.
The dish is often garnished with fresh cilantro or parsley.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef supplies easily absorbable heme iron, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Turmeric and ginger contain curcumin and gingerol, compounds with anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin and coriander stimulate bile production, aiding fat digestion.

items.title: Balanced energy source
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbohydrates makes the dish a well‑rounded source of energy.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Beef can be high in saturated fats; individuals with heart disease should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Salt and soy sauce
items.content: Recipes often include added salt or soy sauce, increasing sodium intake.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some people may be allergic to turmeric, cumin, or ginger.

items.title: Meat safety
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking beef can lead to foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the beef curry hot alongside a generous portion of rice. Add fresh vegetables such as bell peppers or broccoli, and finish with a sprinkle of herbs and a squeeze of lime.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, freeze for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat thoroughly before serving.
